finding.title: Replace ws5_per_profile_test.dart's tautological payload-format assertions with real NotificationGateway verification
finding.why: None of the 3 tests in the 'notification payload format' group ever construct a NotificationGateway or call scheduleDailyReminderForProfile/scheduleStreakAlertForProfile (confirmed: no NotificationGateway( appears anywhere in this file). Two of the three just re-interpolate the same '$dailyReminderPayload:$profileId' formula the source uses and compare it to a literal, or hand-write a `parts` list and assert facts about the literal they just wrote three lines earlier -- these can never fail regardless of what NotificationGateway actually does, so despite the docstring's claim to verify "per-profile payload format", they add file weight without adding protection. The real protection already exists properly (mocked zonedSchedule + captureAny) in the sibling notification_gateway_test.dart:320-416 outside this batch, which is why this is hygiene/redundancy (P3) rather than a live coverage gap.
finding.recommendation: Either delete these two redundant tests (coverage already exists in notification_gateway_test.dart) or rewrite them to construct a NotificationGateway with a mocked FlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin and assert on the captured `payload:` argument from scheduleDailyReminderForProfile, matching this file's own '(good)' ID-allocation tests which do call the real functions.
acceptance_criteria: Remaining payload-format tests in this file (if kept) invoke NotificationGateway rather than re-deriving the expected string independently.
Red-first check: temporarily change the separator/format in notification_gateway.dart's per-profile payload construction and confirm whichever tests remain go red.

finding.why: learning_ledger_dao_test.dart is 446 lines and points_balance_dao_test.dart is 476 lines — both hand-written, both over the AG-3 400-line cap. New split files follow the existing _extra_test.dart/_extended_test.dart naming convention used elsewhere in this directory

finding.title: Replace PinFlowController's raw-English error-string matching with a stable error code

evidence.quote:
String _incorrectPin() => 'Incorrect PIN';
  String _pinsDoNotMatch() => 'PINs do not match';

'Incorrect PIN' => l10n.incorrectPin,
    'PINs do not match' => l10n.pinsDoNotMatch,

finding.why: PinFlowController (no BuildContext/l10n access) emits full English sentences as its error 'codes', and pin_flow_screen.dart's _resolveError matches them by exact string equality to localize. This is the same fragility EH-5 targets one layer up: if a future edit tweaks the wording in one file (e.g. fixes a typo in 'Incorrect PIN'), the switch in the other silently stops matching and falls through to `_ => raw`, showing raw English to Hebrew users with no compiler error to catch the drift.
finding.recommendation: Define a small PinFlowError enum returned/stored instead of a String, and switch on the enum in pin_flow_screen.dart.
acceptance_criteria: PinFlowController exposes a typed error code, not a formatted sentence
A test renaming/removing one of the four magic strings would fail to compile instead of silently breaking localization

finding.title: Extract the duplicated drift .sqlite-suffix delete helper out of AccountLifecycleService and PendingLocalSignupStore
finding.why: Both private _deleteDbFile methods encode the identical drift_flutter '.sqlite'-suffix-with-bare-name-fallback workaround, each discovered and fixed as a separate bug (each carries its own header comment and its own dedicated regression test in this batch: account_lifecycle_db_delete_test.dart and pending_local_signup_file_cleanup_test.dart). Any future drift_flutter version change to the on-disk filename scheme means this exact fix has to be found and reapplied in two places; missing one leaves orphaned .sqlite files on disk or a delete that silently no-ops.
finding.recommendation: Extract one shared deleteDriftDbFile(databasesPath, dbFileName) utility (e.g. under core/database/ or core/utils/) that both services call; keep both existing regression tests but retarget them at the shared utility.
acceptance_criteria: one shared function implements the .sqlite-suffix delete-with-fallback logic
AccountLifecycleService and PendingLocalSignupStore both delegate to it instead of each defining their own copy
both existing regression tests still pass
